merge.title: One FSBL freeze-review package: decide vendor-key policy (Option B either-key, not 2-of-3), FSBL minimum-epoch constant, Merkle-leaf signing, sealed profile, and an HDP-hidden flash counter as a Draft 1.1 review input, before WRP+RDP-2 makes each impossible
merge.threat: The FSBL is the one component that can never be patched after WRP + RDP-2 (invariant #10). Today it embeds exactly one 32-byte C10 vendor key (fsbl/src/vendor_pubkey.rs:20-23) and runs one fpr + one signature check per manifest (fsbl/src/main.rs:335-346). A stolen or coerced vendor key therefore signs firmware every shipped device accepts forever, with RMA as the only fleet remedy. Separately, the anti-rollback floor cannot move: the FSBL reads the rejected unary OTP tally (fsbl/src/otp.rs:1-41), `otp::bump_to` has no production caller, and CMD_FW_COMMIT refuses unconditionally (secure/src/nsc/cmd_fw_commit.rs:332-375), so every release ever signed under the production key stays installable. Finally, a 'bundle verified' receipt says nothing about which FSBL is on the part (#742).
merge.proposal:
Hold ONE recorded FSBL freeze review and write every outcome, including 'declined', into docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md (its 'B accepted or declined at FSBL WRP freeze review' box at :84-97 is still unticked). No item below is implementation-approved; items D and F are inputs to the Draft 1.1/1.2 rollback review only.

A. Vendor-key policy: decide Option B (primary + recovery C10 key, accept EITHER, one signature per manifest) versus A (single key). Do not adopt the 2-of-3 quorum (see dropped parts). Option B costs 32 B of rodata plus a second fpr compare and a second verify only when the primary fails, with zero manifest growth. Record its residual: the FSBL accepts a leaked primary forever.

B. Immutable FSBL minimum-epoch constant (v6 `security_epoch` floor compiled into the FSBL), taken together with A as the doc already recommends (:388-401). Honest scope: it only excludes images signed under the production key before the freeze; it is not a movable floor.

C. Merkle-leaf signing: decide before freeze whether the FSBL verifies `sig(root)` with a bounded proof path (0 nodes = today's behaviour). The v6 manifest has 3,916 B of trailing reserved (fw-manifest/src/v6.rs:90-91), so an 8-node proof fits. The secure-world FW_BEGIN verifier must mirror it. Default to 'declined with record' unless FSBL budget is found: the C10-budget argument is weak (a handful of signatures per release against a 65,536 cap); the real gain is one ceremony per release-set and a cryptographic object for OPEN-REL-1.

D. Rollback backend input to the Draft 1.1 review (FWU-1): put the Trezor U5 shape on the table for OPEN-OTP-1..3 (#543) as an explicit alternative — unary 16-byte cells in a flash page inside HDP1, read and bumped by the pre-PIN stage, hidden via `SECHDPCR.HDP1_ACCDIS` before branch. This directly contradicts a frozen Draft 1.1 MUST and cannot proceed without an owner reopen (see decision_conflicts).

E. Process and tooling with no FSBL cost: (i) #742 — put the FSBL flash digest in every release receipt and the signed release descriptor; (ii) #220 — re-scope the vendor-key OTP hash to a check made by the external SWD verify tool, not by the FSBL on itself; (iii) #225 — freeze the per-vendor-key signature cap in the fwsign ledger before any production signing.

F. Sealed cold-vault profile (no secure-world update after personalization): cost it at the same review as the doc requires (:415-445) and record the outcome. Not a default; today it is a re-architecture, because decoders live in the secure image.

Budget rule for the review: every FSBL byte in A–D competes with the rollback TCB. The Draft candidate links at 38,860 B against a 38,912 B warning limit, i.e. 52 B of margin (fw-rollback-fsbl-resource-map-2026-07.md:153-164). Decide A–D jointly against one measured link, not one at a time.

dropped_parts: BOOT-09 2-of-3 C10 quorum in the FSBL: a second 4008-B signature does not fit the 8 KiB manifest page in either layout (3,995 B / 3,916 B free), so it needs a second manifest page per slot and a change to the frozen geometry registry (geometry/src/lib.rs:121-137, already blocked at #758); it doubles signature verifies on both slots (about +0.75 s worst case on a 2.93 s boot); and the m-of-n committee is a recorded decline (#486, vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:44-50, parity sweep :55).

FSBL self-check of its own embedded key against an OTP hash (BOOT-09 part 2, FWU-9 part 3, as written): a re-flashed FSBL simply omits the check, so it does not close threat-model §9.8 as claimed. Trezor's OTP vendor lock is checked by an immutable stage against a mutable vendor header, which is the opposite trust direction. Only the external-verifier comparison survives, and that tool already diffs the whole FSBL image.
FWU-1 'close #212 as not needed' and 'fold #39 into it': premature; both depend on a backend decision that has not been reopened.
FWU-1 P0 / 'select the backend' framing: rollback work is not implementation-approved (CLAUDE.md) and the backend choice is owner-gated under #543.

FWU-1 claim that an 8 KiB page gives 512 increments as a selling point over OTP: Draft 1.1 makes same-epoch releases cost zero floor writes, so capacity is not the binding constraint; the binding ones are ECC/interrupted-program behaviour and erasability.
FWU-9 `mode-sealed` as a build profile to implement now: the doc says cost it and record, and notes the NS-updatable variant is a substantial re-architecture, not a flag.
FWU-10 optional descriptor-root leaf (PQDESC_V1) in the same tree: roadmap item, no approved format; out of scope for the freeze decision.

FWU-10's own dropped list stands (per-chunk pre-write hash, fix_version soft floor with SE wipe, companion GetFirmwareHash, OptRand anti-klepto, measurement-bound key wrap). The last matches established fact (d) and the doc's do-not-resurface list (:457-466).

live_defects.what: The rollback floor can never rise: FSBL reads the rejected unary OTP tally and no code path writes a floor, so every image ever signed under the vendor key remains installable.
live_defects.evidence: fsbl/src/otp.rs:1-41 (legacy reader, 'not a valid STM32U585 OTP backend'); fsbl/src/main.rs:190,351; secure/src/nsc/cmd_fw_commit.rs:332-375 (fail-closed refusal, no floor write); `bump_to` referenced only in secure/src/hw/otp.rs and tests.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Not shippable today: production is compile-blocked on this (#31 ship-blocker; CLAUDE.md). Known and tracked, not a new finding.

live_defects.what: Single baked vendor key with no recovery path and no OTP/HDP binding; HDP is disabled in the ship profile.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes by design if shipped as is; tracked by #486, #220, #39.

live_defects.what: #220's planned FSBL self-check (embedded key vs OTP hash) would not detect a replaced FSBL, yet threat-model §9.8 presents it as the defence.
live_defects.evidence: docs/security/threat-model.md:517-518; issue #220 body ('FSBL-side boot verify ... halt on mismatch').

merge.residual_after: With Option B accepted: a thief of the primary key can still sign firmware every FSBL accepts forever; recovery only protects devices that install the recovery-signed image first, and a thief of either key wins. With A (single key): unchanged, RMA only. The minimum-epoch constant does not move, so every post-freeze release stays installable until a real rollback backend lands (#31 remains a ship-blocker regardless of this cluster). A valid vendor signature remains authentic, not benign: no item here stops a correctly signed malicious image, and the signature itself remains an exfiltration channel. Merkle signing reduces ceremonies, not key exposure, and adds a parser to the unpatchable stage. If the HDP flash counter were ever adopted, a fault that skips the HDP1_ACCDIS write lets a compromised runtime erase the page and reset the floor, which OTP cannot suffer; before first-boot RDP-2 the page is erasable over SWD (moot, since the whole image is replaceable then). The receipt FSBL digest is evidence about the build, not about a given unit; only the pre-first-power SWD check binds a unit. The sealed profile, if chosen, trades all of the above for RMA or wipe-restore on every parser fix.

skeptic.reason: The core survives: one recorded FSBL freeze review that settles the unticked boxes in docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md (:84-97, :134-135, :388-401, :415-445) is what the repo's own design note asks for, and dropping the 2-of-3 quorum, the FSBL OTP self-check and the 'select backend now' framing is right. The three defect facts check out against code. Not refuted, but several sub-claims are wrong or incomplete: Option B as described cannot work in the field without secure-world and release-gate changes the recommendation never mentions; the budget numbers are a Draft 0.9 proxy and one is stale; items B and C also touch the frozen Draft 1.1; the issue list omits the issue that already owns the measured link (#541); and untracked_delta item 4 is false as written.
skeptic.corrections:
1. Option B is not a 32-byte FSBL change (biggest gap). The secure image holds its own copy of the key (secure/src/fw_update/vendor_pubkey.rs:30-32, 'both binaries must produce byte-identical constants' :5-7). fwsign enforces FSBL == secure == policy (fwsign/src/artifact_key.rs:596-598) and refuses mixed-root artifacts (fwsign/src/subcommands/sign.rs:63). At RDP-2, CMD_FW_* is the only install path (#696), so a shipped secure world that knows only the primary rejects a recovery-signed image at FW_BEGIN. B therefore needs the recovery key in every shipped secure image, an either-key BEGIN verifier, and a reworked artifact gate and policy hash file.

2. The doc's recovery flow (:58-63) is incoherent and the recommendation inherits it. The FSBL re-verifies the manifest signature on every boot against its immutable keys (fsbl/src/main.rs:197-198, :335-346). A 'new primary' that is not in the FSBL can never sign a bootable manifest. After recovery the recovery key becomes the only usable signing key, is no longer cold, and has no successor. State this, or cost a third embedded key.

3. Option B's verify cost is overstated. verify_vendor_fpr runs before verify_signature (main.rs:335-346) and the manifest carries the fingerprint, so the fingerprint selects the key. There is never a second C10 verify; the cost is 32 B plus one more FI-gated fingerprint compare, which is more code than '32 B of rodata'.

4. Missing residual: pick_slot takes the highest fw_version (main.rs:377-382). A leaked-primary holder can sign at the top of the version space, so on any device that takes the attacker's image first, no recovery image can outrank it. The doc's 'recovery key provides a path above it' (:397) fails for those devices.

5. Budget figures. The 38,860 B / 52 B number is a Draft 0.9 proxy (fw-rollback-fsbl-resource-map-2026-07.md:7-19, :153-164); #541 names it as precedent and rules a straddling result non-passing. Option B plus the floor constant (the doc's unmeasured ~40 B) leaves about 12 B on that proxy, i.e. non-passing by #541's rule. '32 KiB with 2,048 B free' is stale: that was before the hw-sha256 swap (fsbl/Cargo.toml:13-15); CLAUDE.md gives a 28,700 B span today, about 4 KiB free.

6. Boot-time figure: filter_valid measured 0.375 s (measured-boot.md:286-296), apparently with only slot A valid, since manifest B was the erased marker page in that run (fsbl/Cargo.toml stage-marker comment). So about 0.375 s per extra C10 verify, and '+0.75 s' for the dropped quorum is a plausible upper bound, not a measurement.

7. Deadline is earlier than the WRP freeze for item A. #541 (FA-G1) freezes a measurement profile with 'a real-size 32-byte vendor key' and blocks #543/#546/#544. The one-key-versus-two decision must be made before that profile freezes, or the warning build measures the wrong FSBL.

8. Item B (minimum-epoch constant) also conflicts with the frozen Draft 1.1, not only D. Draft 1.1 says 'Admission is exactly E > F. F is not a minimum-allowed epoch' (a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:160-161) and already provides factory genesis with E > 1, which establishes the floor in OTP (:2859-2866). A compiled constant is a second floor source and needs the same reopen. Its value is also conditional: the production key does not exist yet (#69), so the constant excludes nothing unless production-signed releases predate a given FSBL build (later batches only). The doc names it FSBL_MIN_ACCEPTED_FW_VERSION (:134, :390), a fw_version in the legacy format; the v6 security_epoch framing and 'needs v6 approval' prerequisite are the merger's addition.

9. Item C (Merkle) changes the exact 121-byte PQFW_V6 signed preimage (fw-manifest/src/v6.rs:55; CLAUDE.md rollback-manifest rule) and uses reserved v6 bytes. That is a Draft 1.1 schema change needing digest review and an owner stage decision, not merely a freeze-review tick. 'Declined with record' is the right default.

10. untracked_delta item 4 is false. docs/architecture/trezor-comparison.md §2.8 (:400-417) records Trezor's SECRET-region flash monoctr with the verdict 'RE-EVALUATE AFTER DRAFT-1.1 CANDIDATE GATES ... a possible supporting durable-stage mechanism, not a substitute authority'. Only the HDP1_ACCDIS-hidden framing is new, and §2.8 is a second recorded position against D. The parity-sweep wording 'OTP monoctr' (:55) is still loose.

11. Item D feasibility: the manifest pages are rewritten at runtime by the updater, so the counter page cannot share or replace Manifest A at page 5. D needs a full registry shift (geometry v7, #752) and the bank-2 HDP2 mirror (#43). The stated residual (skipped ACCDIS write lets runtime erase the page) is correct. Keep D strictly as a note into #543.

12. Item E(ii) is hollow as kept. The recommendation concedes the SWD verifier already diffs the whole FSBL image, so an OTP hash adds nothing. Better action: decline or close #220 with that reason and fix threat-model.md §9.8 (:517-518) to cite invariant #10's SWD check as the defence.

13. Custody prerequisite is understated. Per the #486 triage comment, the firmware vendor key today is a passphrase-encrypted blob (fwsign/src/keystore.rs), with no HSM mandate; #67's HSM key is a different (factory manifest) key. 'Colder custody' for a recovery key is undefined until #69 defines any custody.

14. Priority and cost: split them. Item A is P1 because of the #541 ordering. B, C, E, F are P2; D is P3 review input. The review record itself is S; accepting Option B is M once the secure-world and fwsign changes are counted.

live_defect.evidence: Entry 1 (floor can never rise): CONFIRMED. fsbl/src/otp.rs:1-41 reads the rejected unary tally; cmd_fw_commit.rs:332-375 refuses with no floor write; bump_to appears only in secure/src/hw/otp.rs and tests; cmd_fw_begin.rs:112 reads the same floor. Nuance: because COMMIT always refuses, no update activates through the handler at all, and pick_slot's highest-version rule (main.rs:377-382) gives incidental downgrade resistance while a newer valid slot exists. Entry 2 (single key, no recovery): facts CONFIRMED (vendor_pubkey.rs:20-23, main.rs:335-346), but it is a design residual, not a defect — Option A is the documented default. Its 'no OTP/HDP binding' wording is misleading: this cluster itself shows the OTP self-check is useless, and HDP protects secrets, not a public key. HDP absence itself is confirmed (no SECHDPCR/SECWM1R2 code; production-security.md:525-531). Entry 3 (#220 claim drift): CONFIRMED, low. threat-model.md:517-518 presents the OTP hash as the defence against a re-flashed FSBL, and #220's body includes the FSBL self-verify; nothing is implemented.
